question: Why does MSTR earn REJECTED at $77.80 after breaking its $79.00 stop, sub-1.0x mNAV, and Stage 4 trend floors?

epigraph.quote: The goal is to double Bitcoin per share in seven years through the use of digital credit.

web_blocks.html: Strategy Inc. houses two unequal engines under one ticker. Its Software segment ($372.10 million 9M 2026 revenue) is growing cloud subscriptions but remains cash-negative before treasury interest. Its Bitcoin segment holds 850,849 coins (~99% of assets), funded by $6.75 billion of convertible debt and $13.48 billion of adjusted preferred liquidation preference. At the November 20, 2026 close of $77.80 ($58,798.98 Bitcoin), MSTR sits in Stage 4 below 1.00x mNAV, earning a clean REJECTED verdict. [2][42][50][54]

web_blocks.html: Three facts separate this November 20 refresh from our November 12 review. First, Bitcoin's drop to $58,798.98 pushed Strategy's holdings 22.1% below its $75,452 average cost and compressed EV/BTC mNAV to 0.972x. Issuing equity below 1.0x mNAV dilutes common holders—and November 2 to 15 Form 8-Ks already show 74.7% of ATM proceeds paying off 12% STRC preferreds instead of buying Bitcoin. Second, MSCI's expected November 2026 exclusion threatens forced passive outflows. Third, MSTR broke its $79.00 stop on 1.95x volume, leaving zero support below. [2][38][42][50][54]

web_blocks.title: THE SINGLE HINGE
paragraphs: Can Strategy restore positive Bitcoin-per-share yield and cover $1.51 billion to $1.59 billion of annual fixed charges without dilutive common sales or Bitcoin liquidation? Until filings prove it, new capital stays out. [2][12][50]

book_paragraphs: Strategy Inc. combines an established analytics software business with a leveraged Bitcoin treasury engine. Effective Q2 2026, management split GAAP reporting into Software and Bitcoin segments. Software generated $372.10 million in nine-month revenue with rapid cloud subscription growth, yet remained cash-negative before treasury interest. Meanwhile, the Bitcoin segment represents roughly 99% of assets—850,849 Bitcoin backed by $6.750 billion in convertible debt and $13.484 billion in adjusted preferred stock preference. [2][50]

At the November 20, 2026 close of $77.80, the stock trades below static asset coverage and in a confirmed Stage 4 markdown. Bitcoin closed the same day at $58,798.98, leaving Strategy's holdings 22.1% below its $75,452 average purchase price. Our November 20 asset bridge puts static residual common value at $81.13 per share—or $77.51 after one year of $1.55 billion preferred dividend and interest burn—placing EV-to-Bitcoin mNAV at 0.972x. [2][50][54]

Falling below 1.00x mNAV breaks the core premise of the Strategy equity story. Selling Class A shares below net asset value shrinks Bitcoin per share, and November Form 8-K filings already show 74.7% of common ATM proceeds diverted to buy back 12% STRC preferred stock. Add expected November 2026 MSCI index exclusion, $5.914 billion in 2027–2028 convertible cash puts, and a 32.0% weekly drop through our prior $79.00 stop, and the honest verdict is REJECTED. [2][38][42][50]

Both our 12-month Base fair value of $76.34 and our probability-weighted value of $66.86 sit below the $77.80 market price. The consolidated positions ledger confirms zero MSTR and zero MSTX shares held, making the holding action NOT_HELD. Keep 100% of marginal capital in cash during this broad-market Downtrend until MSTR forms a real base, repairs its trend, and proves positive per-share Bitcoin compounding.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When the financing flywheel flips from accretive to dilutive and the chart slices through its structural stop, rejecting the stock is discipline, not pessimism.
